title: Home-loving, non-drinking Joe and the sugar water
summary: Joe stayed home, did not drink, kidded people, and drank sugar water in restaurants. Stella doubts he was diabetic.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: If you wasn't a kid out there, don't stop at Joe. Because he could kid you and he'd make you so mad. And he never got mad. But he just liked a kid. He liked a kid. And everything was good natured with him. He wasn't hardly serious with anything. But he loved his home. He did. He loved his home. He was a man that didn't stay out all night. Gallivanting around. Because Lily used to tell me all the time. Joe said, I got to go home to that chicken. He called me the chicken all the time. He says, I got to go home to that chicken. He never would stay out. He wasn't a drinking man. Fall from it.
Somebody told me about that. He used to like that sugar water. Just put sugar in water.

Yes. Sometimes when he'd go out to eat or he'd be caught on the road. He'd always eat the Chinaman food. He liked that. He liked that because he could go away and the sugar bowl was on the table. And then he would keep the sugar bowl right by him. And get a great big glass and water would never get out of that glass. He'd keep adding water and sugar until he had enough. It would be lemonade or anything just plain water. No, just plain sugar water. Plain sugar water.
Somebody told me they wondered maybe if he had diabetes or something when he used all that sugar. Do you think that he had any trouble at that time?
